title: Truncation and heart theorem for t-admissible condensed coefficients
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], and put $R=\Gamma(*,\Lambda)$. Assume that $R$ is regular coherent, meaning that every finitely generated ideal is finitely presented and every finitely presented $R$-module has a finite resolution by finitely generated projective $R$-modules, and that $R\to\Gamma(S,\Lambda)$ is flat for every extremally disconnected profinite set $S$ (a compact Hausdorff totally disconnected space in which the closure of every open set is open). These two assumptions are the meaning of t-admissibility here.

Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] with Zariski locally finitely many irreducible components. On its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] put $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. In the ambient derived category $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda_X)$ of sheaves of $\Lambda_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], use ordinary derived tensor and unit $\Lambda_X[0]$. Let $D_{\mathrm{lis}}(X,\Lambda)$ denote its full subcategory of dualizable objects, where dualizable means admitting evaluation and coevaluation with the two triangle identities.

The ambient standard truncation functors $\tau^{\le n}$ and $\tau^{\ge n}$ preserve $D_{\mathrm{lis}}(X,\Lambda)$ for every $n\in\mathbf Z$. They define the restriction of the ambient standard t-structure to this subcategory. Its heart is exactly the sheaves pro-etale locally isomorphic to
$$\Lambda_X\otimes_{\underline R}\underline N$$
for finitely presented $R$-modules $N$; the module $N$ may depend on the member of the cover. Here $\underline R$ and $\underline N$ are constant sheaves with discrete coefficients, and the tensor uses the canonical constant-section map $\underline R\to\Lambda_X$. In particular every cohomology sheaf of a dualizable object has this local form.

source.place: Definition 6.1 and Theorem 6.2(2), with Definition 3.3(1) and the notation of Section 3. This is the general t-admissible-ring theorem, not its field specialization.

proof.text:
The scalar hypothesis has the following consequences. For a perfect $R$-complex $P$, choose a bounded finite-projective representative [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. Since $R$ is coherent, [lem-sc-coherent-ring-perfect-complex-cohomology] makes every $H^q(P)$ finitely presented. By the assumed finite projective resolutions, each $H^q(P)[0]$ is perfect. Write $[a,b]$ for a cohomological bound of $P$. For any $n$, induct on $j$ from $a-1$ to $\min(n,b)$ using
$$\tau^{\le j-1}P\longrightarrow\tau^{\le j}P\longrightarrow H^j(P)[-j]\longrightarrow(\tau^{\le j-1}P)[1].$$
The base object is zero. The first and third objects at each induction step are perfect, so the middle object is perfect by the shift-and-cone closure in [lem-sf-perfect-ring-classical-generator]. This proves that $\tau^{\le n}P$ is perfect, including $n<a$ and $n\ge b$. The triangle $\tau^{\le n-1}P\to P\to\tau^{\ge n}P$ then proves the same for $\tau^{\ge n}P$. In particular finitely presented modules placed in degree zero are perfect, and perfect scalar complexes have finitely presented cohomology.

source.place: Proposition 6.6, implication (2) to (1); finite cohomological induction spelling out the truncation argument

proof.text:
For any scheme $T$, set $L_T(Q)=\Lambda_T\otimes^L_{\underline R}\underline Q$. We check the flat comparison on the affine w-contractible basis, which exists by [sk-thm-pe-weakly-contractible-basis]. For such $V\to T$, [lem-zl-wcontractible-condensed-scalar-evaluation] gives $A_V=\Gamma(V,\Lambda_V)=\Gamma(\pi_0 V,\Lambda)$, t-exact derived sections, and $R\Gamma(V,L_TQ)=Q\otimes_R^L A_V$. The space $\pi_0 V$ is extremally disconnected profinite, so the stated t-admissibility makes $A_V$ flat over $R$. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact], termwise tensor with $A_V$ preserves the kernel, image and cokernel sequences defining cohomology. Hence it preserves acyclic complexes and computes derived tensor, with $H^q(Q\otimes_R^L A_V)=H^q(Q)\otimes_R A_V$. The same kernel/cokernel calculation identifies the canonical truncation comparisons after evaluation at $V$. By [det-pe-sections-conservative] these comparisons are isomorphisms on sheaves. Thus, for either truncation,
$$\tau^{\le n}L_T(Q)\simeq L_T(\tau^{\le n}Q),\qquad \tau^{\ge n}L_T(Q)\simeq L_T(\tau^{\ge n}Q),$$
and $\mathcal H^q(L_TQ)\cong\Lambda_T\otimes_{\underline R}\underline{H^q(Q)}$. The ordinary tensor here is the degree-zero cokernel defining scalar extension. This argument does not require a finite-component hypothesis on $T$.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 6.2, the evaluation of the last comparison at w-contractible affines; equations (3.1)–(3.2)

proof.text: Let $K$ be dualizable on the given $X$. By [lem-zl-condensed-dualizable-local-perfect-models], choose a pro-etale cover on which $K|_{U_i}\simeq L_{U_i}(P_i)$ with $P_i$ perfect over $R$. The cover is not required to have a uniform scalar complex or a uniform amplitude. By [lem-sfb-alpha-iso], restriction identifies the coefficient rings. Restriction to these site objects is exact on module sheaves, using the identified-coefficient inverse image of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]; on complexes this preserves kernels and cokernels, hence standard truncations and cohomology. Step 2 therefore identifies $(\tau^{\le n}K)|_{U_i}$ with $L_{U_i}(\tau^{\le n}P_i)$, and likewise for $\tau^{\ge n}$. Step 1 makes both scalar truncations perfect. The reverse implication of [lem-zl-condensed-dualizable-local-perfect-models], applied on $X$ to these local models, makes both ambient truncations dualizable. This proves preservation for every integer $n$, without assuming that the cover objects themselves have finitely many irreducible components.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 6.2(2), application of Theorem 4.13 and Proposition 6.6

proof.text: The full dualizable subcategory is stable by [lem-zl-condensed-dualizable-local-perfect-models]. Set $D_{\mathrm{lis}}^{\le0}=D_{\mathrm{lis}}\cap D^{\le0}$ and $D_{\mathrm{lis}}^{\ge0}=D_{\mathrm{lis}}\cap D^{\ge0}$. The ambient orthogonality and shift inclusions hold on these full subcategories. By Step 3, the ambient triangle $\tau^{\le0}K\to K\to\tau^{\ge1}K$ lies in $D_{\mathrm{lis}}$, so it supplies the required t-decomposition there. These are precisely the axioms of the restricted standard t-structure. Its heart consists of the dualizable objects concentrated in degree zero.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 6.2(2), inheritance of the t-structure once truncations preserve lisse objects

proof.text:
Suppose a module sheaf $M[0]$ is dualizable. Choose local scalar perfect models $M|_{U_i}\simeq L_{U_i}(P_i)$ by [lem-zl-condensed-dualizable-local-perfect-models]. Take degree-zero cohomology and use the exact restriction in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] and Step 2 to obtain
$$M|_{U_i}\cong\Lambda_{U_i}\otimes_{\underline R}\underline{H^0(P_i)}.$$
By [lem-sc-coherent-ring-perfect-complex-cohomology], each $N_i=H^0(P_i)$ is finitely presented. This proves the asserted local form for the heart; it does not require $P_i$ itself to be concentrated in degree zero.

source.place: Theorem 6.2(2), description of the heart using equation (6.2)

proof.text: Conversely, let $M$ have the stated local form with finitely presented modules $N_i$. Their assumed finite resolutions make $N_i[0]$ perfect by [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. Step 2 identifies $L_{U_i}(N_i[0])$ with the ordinary module sheaf $\Lambda_{U_i}\otimes_{\underline R}\underline{N_i}$ in degree zero. The reverse implication of [lem-zl-condensed-dualizable-local-perfect-models] on $X$ now makes $M[0]$ dualizable, hence an object of the restricted heart. Finally, for any dualizable $K$ and integer $j$, Step 3 applied twice and shift closure give $\mathcal H^j(K)[0]\simeq(\tau^{\ge j}\tau^{\le j}K)[j]$ dualizable. The forward heart description in Step 5 applies to this sheaf. Different $N_i$, zero modules, and varying ranks are all allowed.

source.place: Theorem 6.2(2), reverse heart inclusion and cohomology consequence

proof_origin.place: Theorem 6.2(2), proof, using Theorem 4.13 and Proposition 6.6. The scalar finite Postnikov induction and the flat kernel/image/cokernel calculation are expanded explicitly.
